body: Namibia primarily uses yellow front and back licence plates. Vanity plates are white with blue lettering.
Namibia drives on the left side of the road. Note: This is also true for other countries in southern and eastern Africa. Middle Eastern countries with coverage drive on the right.

All Namibian coverage was taken with a white pickup truck with a short antenna leaning slightly to the left. No other southern African country has a similar car; Oman has a similar car but antenna leans right.
Most roads use single yellow outer lines and white centre lines. Other southern African countries also use single yellow outer lines.
Namibia uses green directional signs with yellow road numbers. Road categories include A, B, C, D, M, and sometimes F roads. South Africa uses N and R roads.
Namibia's German colonial history is evident in place names and some older buildings with German architectural style.
Small stone bollards can be found at intersections and road sides.
Round metal bins, often green and white like the Nigerian flag, appear at rest stops and intersections. Some bins are blue and white.
Coverage is mostly on main roads, with sparse coverage on minor roads.
A map shows pavement type and driving direction on major roads.
Namibian area codes help determine regions or cities on urban rounds.

Knowing where the Google car is blurred helps narrow location: the blurred car is only northwest of Ondangwa in the north; unpaved roads with blurred cars indicate side roads or towns; paved roads like between Nordoewer and Aussenkehr have unblurred cars. Note: Blurred car correlates with 2024 copyright, use cautiously.
Roads flanked by tall, lush trees generally indicate northern Namibia; greener and more trees suggest farther north-northeast.
A pocket around Oshakati has more agricultural land with light sandy soil; associated with Hyphaene Petersiana fan palms.
Landscape east of Windhoek resembles Botswana’s with flat, dry terrain, reddish soil, golden grass, shrubbery, and acacia trees.
Dry mountains & hills dominate western and southern Namibia.
Further northwest, greener regions feature hills & mountains covered in shrubbery and trees.
A lush pocket south of Tsumeb with green grass and mountains.
Near Windhoek a dry rolling hill landscape with yellow grass and dead-looking shrubs & small trees.
Coastal sandy landscape with occasional dunes near and north of Swakopmund, and pockets near Luderitz and Oranjemund.
Southeast Namibia features many small NW-SE ridges; roads over them appear bumpy with valleys between ridges.
Tall pink sand dunes are mainly east of Sossusvlei and visible from farther roads.
Vineyards occur exclusively around Aussenkehr bordering South Africa.
Agricultural fields just west of Mariental have somewhat uniform patterns.
Road A1 between Windhoek and Okahandja is one of two divided major Namibian roads; another is southeast of Swakopmund with dry coastal terrain.
Road B1 south of Grunau passes desolate desert landscape with low, dry vegetation.
B1 sections near Grunau to Keetmanshoop have deteriorated road quality and hillier terrains; some cloudy sections near Keetmanshoop and flat stretches between Gibeon and Mariental.
Road between Gibeon and Tses has wider shoulders and excellent pavement quality.
B1 between Mariental and Rehoboth features generic arid steppe, paved road, NW bound angle, with sun in SE.
Near Rehoboth, vegetation and hills increase approaching Windhoek with pointed hills and ridges visible; weather partly cloudy.
North of Okahandja, B1 is generally flat with occasional hills, short golden grass, green acacias; sun shines to N-NW and two distinctive pointy mountains west of the road.
B2 NE of Swakopmund distinguished by sandy soil, mountain ridge east, lone hills NW, and hazy skies near Swakopmund.
Between Karibib and Usakos, sunrise coverage with thin clouds, mountains north and smaller hills south.
East of Karibib, clear weather, distant mountains, wide shoulders, and E-NE road angle.
Desolate paved road with flat, dry landscape, green shrubbery, and hills east; eastwards driving distinguishes it from B4.
B4 east of Luderitz features bright sandy soil, flat terrain near road, distant hills, becoming hillier near Luderitz; railway south along most of the stretch.
East of Aus, road winds through table-topped mountains; similar but redder and closer mountains east of D432 intersection.
Post Kuibis plateau, flat landscape with gradual incline, very red soil, limited shrubbery, and clear skies with distant clouds.
Between Seeheim and Keetmanshoop, flat terrain with nearby mountains, ridges, and a closely-following southern railway.
B6 east from Windhoek ranges from hilly to flat; orange soil with green vegetation; no clear skies along the road.
B8 has light grainy pavement, E-NE angle, and vegetated northern landscapes.
Bright soil, cloud-covered skies, and a tabletop mountain ridge mark this paved N-NW bound road.
C14 is unpaved, cloud-covered (north), becoming clear near south; similar landscapes south of Bethanien are paved.
C19 marked by very red soil, golden grass tufts, and mostly dark clouds.
C22 paved east road with freshly cut orange grass tufts and large rocky hills nearby; low sun east is helpful for ID.
C13 features large rugged mountains west, light and orange soils contrasting with green shrubbery; wispy clouds sometimes hide the sun in east.
C34 looks like dark streaked black sand surrounded by more sand with coastal shrubbery and coast visible; white bollards with yellow front and red back reflectors line the road.
Northern C35 marked by red tinted grainy pavement and green savannah-like grass under low cumulus clouds.
South of C41 intersection, road quality worsens and landscape becomes sandy with hidden hills; S-SE bound with scattered cirrostratus and cumulus clouds.
Near Kamanjab, green hilly landscape features impressive cloud formations and orange hues on horizon.
Rugged mountain formations appear to the west of C35 and side roads.
C38 is a northern paved road with sandy soil, green vegetation, short grass, and spotty clouds; sun faintly shines north.
C39 travels through wide valleys with vegetation-covered hills, N-NE road angle, and dotted sunny sky with cumulus clouds.
C40 has NW angle on flat terrain with short grass, trees, and cumulus clouds; sun sets west near Kamanjab.
East of C35 intersection, grainy pavement with soft grass and sandy soil under cumulus clouds; west of C35 is hillier with changing road angle.
C43 has impressive red-colored tabletop mountains; wide unpaved road with light gravel contrasts red landscape.
C44 is a wide, sandy unpaved road with E-SE orientation; D3301 further south looks similar but has redder soil and eastbound traffic.
C47 is a wider unpaved road with slightly redder soil, NE bound with SW driving direction; clear or wispy cloud skies.
C49 panhandle section has poor pavement, faded or missing white road lines, red tinted pavement, and low western sun with clear skies.
D3600 and unlabelled road NE to Mpungu have light grainy pavement with faded yellow lines; roads run N-S or NE through northern landscape.
Some northern roads lack yellow outer lines; C46 goes NW to SE, E-W section near Ruacana has poor pavement, with sun low to NW; other roads vary in vegetation and sun angle.
Windhoek is Namibia’s largest city with many high rises downtown, affluent gated neighborhoods on hills, white street signs, and slums to the northwest.
Gobabis is a large north-south gridded desert city with red soil, mostly unpaved roads, some vegetation, green framed street signs, and blue bins.
Swakopmund and Walvis Bay are flat coastal cities with sandy streets, palms and Norfolk pines, square signposts, white and blue bins in Swakopmund, and yellow lamps downtown.
Henties Bay is less gridded and poorer than Swakopmund, with mostly unpaved roads and occasional yellow lamps.
Longstrand is a small resort town with pink brick sidewalks and overcast, gloomy weather.
Luderitz has light rocky hillsides surrounding the hilly coastal town.
Oranjemund is a wealthy gridded city with east-west streets, abundant vegetation, Norfolk pines, and street signs marked on small blue markers.
Aussenkehr features orange thatched fences, walls, and huts on a hillside.
Thatched architecture also occurs in Noordoewer, built on flat land with an imposing cliff southwest in South Africa.
Rosh Pinah is identifiable by dry mountains northeast and southwest of the city.
Aus features rocky, dry hills with smooth northern slopes and rugged southern peaks.
Most streets in Rundu have deep light-colored sandy surfaces with tire tracks.
Opuwo is surrounded by orange mountains covered in green vegetation with great mountain views.
Otavi sits amid many distant mountains with reddish sandy soil and a green landscape on a northeast-southwest grid.
From Karibib, the dark silhouette of Erongo Mountain is to the north, with dry shrubbery-covered hills south.
Usakos neighbors a lone tall ridge with a rugged texture to SSE and a smaller red-tinted mountain east or northeast; Erongo Mountain’s cliffs are visible from north.
Mt Brandeburg’s crown-like shape is visible northwest from Uis, surrounded by dry hills and distinct white open-pit mines to the west.
Ariamsvlei is recognized by a flat-topped hill with rocky ridgelines to north or east and dark red soil with bushes and small trees surrounding it.
